items.summary: The Canadian climate Minister's reluctance to openly commit to cooperation with the EU on its climate policy stems from the fact that Ottawa is effectively seeking an exemption from the bloc's carbon border tax, according to a December 2025 internal document seen by Euronews.

items.title: One dead, 2 injured in fiery, multi-vehicle crash in Whitby: OPP
items.summary: A 20-year-old is facing impaired driving charges after one person was killed and two others were injured in a fiery, three-vehicle crash in Whitby Sunday night, provincial police say.

items.title: Britain says many migrants will have to wait longer to win the right to stay
items.summary: The British government announced Monday that it will double the time many immigrants must wait before they can settle permanently in the country, though it exempted key workers and high earners from the changes.

items.title: Ministry alleges thousands of OSAP applications came from single IP address
items.summary: At two career colleges now under the Ontario government's microscope, more than half of the thousands of student financial aid applications last year came from a single IP address, officials allege in documents filed in court.

items.title: Canadian police urge caution after reports of tampered Halloween candy
items.summary: Police across Canada are urging caution after several reports of families finding tampered Halloween candy in Alberta, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec and Nova Scotia.

items.title: U.S. judge dismisses Trump election lawsuit in Alaska
items.summary: A federal judge on Sunday threw out a lawsuit by U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration seeking to block Alaska from certifying a loss by Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Tuesday’s midterm elections if votes for a rival who shares his name could have changed the outcome.
